Subject: Eastwood RFP — Appendix A: data classification & deid flow

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the quick intake on the RFP. Appendix A asks for a step-by-step description of how Redwood handles incoming PHI, including: initial classification, routing to de-identification, what fields are removed vs tokenized, auditability of the deid process, and how we ensure no re-identification in downstream logs/backups.

Could you send a short narrative and a diagram we can include in our submission? The procurement team also asked whether you support configurable deid templates (PII-only, full-PHI tokenization, pseudo-anonymization) and if the deid stage can be applied before tokens are persisted in any storage.

We are on a tight timeline — submission due 2027-05-28. Appreciate any attachments you can share.

Best,

Subject: Re: Fwd: Eastwood RFP — Appendix A: data classification & deid flow

Laura / Evelyn,

Draft attached. I kept the language non-product-legal while preserving accuracy for technical reviewers. Highlights below (TL;DR first):

- Ingress classification: rules-based classifier (regex + ML models) applied at the API gateway. Configurable per-tenant policy that tags incoming fields as PII/PHI/metadata. Classification happens in-memory; raw payloads are held only on the serving VM memory during evaluation.

- De-identification stage: executed as a deterministic pipeline step before any persistence. Supported modes:
  1) Redaction (irreversible removal)
  2) Tokenization (deterministic pseudonymization with customer-scoped tokens stored in an HSM-backed token vault optional)
  3) Pseudo-anonymization (one-way hashing + salt)

- Templates: We ship three vetted templates out-of-the-box (PII-only, PHI-minimization, Full-PHI-tokenization). Customers can provide custom templates; templates are versioned and tied to model/config rollouts.

- Storage & logs: We never persist raw PHI to long-term object storage in hosted mode. Short-lived caches (KV caches, batch buffers) are purged per policy; retention windows configurable. Audit logs record deid decisions (template id, rule matched, timestamp, request id) but do not contain substituted original PHI values.

- Re-identification risk controls: deterministic tokenization uses tenant-specific keys; tokens cannot be reversed without access to token vault and corresponding key. For hosted customers requiring stronger isolation, dedicated capacity and private deployments allow customer-managed KMS/HSM so token vault keys never leave customer control.

- Evidence & verification: we provide a deid_workflow diagram (attached), sample audit log extracts (redacted), and a short test plan for Eastwood to run a verification sweep.

Attachments: EWS_RFP_AppA_Deid_Questions.pdf (answers mapped to their question list), deid_workflow_v3.drawio.png, redwood_deid_playbook_v1.pdf (internal playbook, sanitized)

Notes / open items for Legal: we should confirm whether we can share the sanitized sample audit logs with the RFP; I removed any real request ids.

If this looks good I can convert to a one-page narrative for Appendix A.

— Rishi
Technical Lead, Inference Privacy & Controls

Laura — thank you, and please pass my thanks to Rishi. The attachments look good. A couple of follow-ups:

1) For tokenization: can you confirm whether token vault access logs (for token reversal) are included in audit exports? Our security team wants to see who accessed the vault and when.
2) For hosted customers, you say raw PHI is not persisted — can you state whether any telemetry or model gradients might be generated that could leak PHI? We need a plain sentence describing model training/telemetry policy.

Also — can Eastwood request a private deployment demo where the token vault is customer-managed? That would be helpful for CISO-level review.

Best,
Sara
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eastwood RFP — Appendix A: data classification & deid flow

Laura / Rishi — legal review notes: we can provide a one-page Appendix A narrative plus the sanitized evidence items referenced. Confirmations:

- Token vault access logs: yes, we can include access logs metadata (timestamp, principal id, action) in audit exports without including secret key material. For hosted customers, access to token reversal is restricted to SRE/ops with just-in-time approval flows; we can flag that in the narrative.

- Model training/telemetry: we do not use customer request data to train public models. Telemetry (latencies, error rates, token counts) is aggregated and does not contain request payloads. For enterprise/private deployments, customers can opt out of any telemetry export.

- BAA status & timeline: Legal can sign a standard BAA. For Eastwood we should propose a BAA execution within two weeks after LOI — Legal will prepare language about audit rights and subprocessor disclosures.

I will prepare a short legal paragraph to append to the narrative. Rishi — please remove the internal playbook PDF from the artifacts we attach to the customer-facing Appendix and only include the sanitized PDF and diagram.

— Evelyn
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
